preconditions: a2 (the caller filename) must be non-null and its first byte must be non-'\0'; otherwise the function returns -1 before touching this.

this must be a valid object whose base holds the 12-byte magic header and whose buffer at this+0x14 is large enough for the filename plus its null terminator; the copy loop has no explicit bounds check.
The global search-count dword_8B8E30 and the audio-entry directory array byte_8B5A3C (stride 0x84) must be initialized before the fallback open loop is reached.
postconditions: On success (returns 0): the caller filename is copied verbatim into this+0x14; this+0x10 holds the open file handle; the 12-byte header at this+0x00 was read and matched one of aCubemas410/aCubemas400/aCubemas401; three 4-byte header fields are read at this+0x114, this+0x118 and this+0x120; this+0x11C is set to (field@this+0x118 << 8); a buffer of that size is allocated and its pointer stored at this+0x128; the payload is read into it; this+0x11C is then incremented by 24.

On return -2: the file could not be opened either at the direct path or through any of the dword_8B8E30 audio-entry directories; an 'Error opening MAS file %s' message is logged via sub_53C590(-2, ...).

On return -1: either a2 was null/empty, the 12-byte magic header matched none of the three cube-map signatures, or the buffer allocation failed; on the header/allocation failure paths the file handle at this+0x10 is closed via FileCloseWithLock and an error message is logged via sub_53C590(-1, ...).
side_effects: Writes the object fields this+0x14 (filename), this+0x10 (file handle), this+0x00 (12-byte magic header), this+0x114, this+0x118, this+0x120, this+0x11C and this+0x128.
Opens a file handle on success that outlives this call and is owned by the object (closed only on the header-mismatch and allocation-failure error paths).
Allocates a heap buffer via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper whose pointer is stored at this+0x128; the buffer is not freed in this function.
Calls sub_589901 on this+0x14 to normalize/prepare the filename before the open attempt.
Reads from the opened file: a 12-byte header, three 4-byte header fields, and the payload block of size (field@this+0x118 << 8).
Logs errors through sub_53C590 on the -1 and -2 paths.

external_dependencies.name: file I/O wrappers (sub_587DB0 open, sub_5803F read, sub_587D02 close)

disputes.description: The object class CubeMapMasFileLoader comes only from the packet IR's DERIVED proposal (function:0x0055FC40, caller:0x0053CBC0). This single function shows no constructor, vtable or ownership proof; the name is a working label, not an established type.

this+0x00 is read as a 12-byte header and compared with strcmp against three magic strings, but the same location is the base of the object; whether the magic occupies the whole 0x00..0x0C extent or shares it with other members is unresolved, so only the 0x00 dword is declared in layouts.

unresolved: Meaning of the three 4-byte header fields read from the file into this+0x114, this+0x118 and this+0x120: only the field at this+0x118 feeds the data-size computation (field << 8); the purposes of the other two are unknown.
Purpose of the trailing +24 adjustment to this+0x11C after the payload read is unknown.
The role of global aSS_3 (0x005C2D64) is unknown; it appears in the packet evidence but is not visible in the raw source body, so it is not promoted to globals.
Object class owning this layout is unproven; the fields are consistent with a cube-map/MAS loader object but the identity is DERIVED at best.
sub_589901's exact normalization semantics are unknown; it may modify this+0x14 in place before the open attempt.

The file I/O wrappers (sub_587DB0, sub_5803F, sub_587D02), StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck (sub_5815F) and OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper (sub_587C03) are cut edges marked compiler_runtime; their identities as fopen/fread/fclose/vsprintf/malloc equivalents are inferred from use, not confirmed.
Whether the file handle at this+0x10 is eventually closed by a sibling method (this function only closes it on error) cannot be shown from this packet alone.
tests_required: Guard: null or empty a2 returns -1 without touching any this field.

Direct open success: handle stored at this+0x10, 12-byte magic validated, three header fields read, dataSize = (field@this+0x118 << 8), buffer allocated at this+0x128, payload read, this+0x11C += 24, returns 0.
Fallback open: direct path fails, first matching byte_8B5A3C entry (stride 0x84) yields a handle stored at this+0x10.
Total open failure: returns -2 and logs 'Error opening MAS file %s' via sub_53C590(-2, ...).
Header mismatch: returns -1, closes the handle via FileCloseWithLock, logs via sub_53C590(-1, ...).
Allocation failure: returns -1, closes the handle, logs aUnableToAlloca via sub_53C590(-1, ...).
